cards.text: Friend, this whole book is one short letter. It's from Paul the apostle (Romans 1:1), writing with Timothy, who he calls our brother. And it's going to a man named Philemon, who Paul calls "our beloved fellow worker."

cards.question: Before anything else, Paul tells Philemon what he is right now. How does Paul describe himself?

answers.text: A servant of the church in Rome
A shepherd of the flock in Ephesus

cards.text: Paul's got more names on the envelope. He greets Apphia, "our sister," and Archippus, "our fellow soldier," so friend, this man just added HALF the neighborhood to the group chat.

cards.question: Paul also writes to a whole church along with Apphia and Archippus. Where does that church meet?

cards.text: Then comes Paul's blessing: "Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ." Now he turns to Philemon himself.

cards.question: Paul tells Philemon he only thanks God for him once in a while.
Paul says he thanks God because of what he keeps hearing about Philemon. What does he hear about?

answers.text: His faith in Jesus and love for the saints
His big gifts to the poor and the widows
His bold preaching in the towns nearby

cards.text: Paul prays that Philemon's partnership in the faith becomes effective. Then he says Philemon's love gives him great joy and encouragement.

cards.question: Paul tells Philemon that he has refreshed the hearts of the saints.

cards.text: Philemon's the guy who walks in and the whole room breathes easier, like a warm batch coming out on a LONG day. But now Paul turns a corner: in Christ, he says, he's bold enough to order Philemon to do what is proper.

cards.question: Paul could just give Philemon the order. Instead, he says he would rather ___ on the basis of love.

cards.text: Then Paul adds: "For I, Paul, am now aged, and a prisoner of Christ Jesus as well." An older man in chains asking NICELY, friend, who's saying no to that?
And here it is, friend, the reason for the whole letter. Paul's appealing to Philemon for someone named Onesimus, who Paul calls "my child."

cards.question: Paul calls Onesimus his child. When does Paul say he became a father to Onesimus?
Paul gets honest about Onesimus. Formerly he was ___ to Philemon, but now he has become ___ both to Philemon and to Paul.

cards.text: Useless to useful, friend, that's MY whole life story after years in a junk drawer. And now Paul says he's sending Onesimus back, calling him "my very heart."

cards.question: Paul says he would have liked to keep Onesimus with him, to help him while he's in chains for the gospel.

cards.text: No sneaking around it. Paul says he didn't want to do anything without Philemon's consent.

cards.question: Why does Paul want Philemon's consent before doing anything about Onesimus?

answers.text: So his goodness is by his own free will
So the church can settle it all together
So the authorities won't punish Paul for it

cards.text: Then Paul looks at the whole thing from a new angle. He says perhaps this is why Onesimus was separated from Philemon for a while.

cards.question: Separated for a while, Paul says, so that Philemon might have Onesimus back for ___.
And not as a slave anymore. Paul says Philemon will have Onesimus back as a beloved ___.

cards.text: Paul says Onesimus is especially beloved to him, but even more so to Philemon, both in person and in the Lord. Then Paul brings up their partnership.

cards.question: Paul says that if Philemon considers him a partner, he should receive Onesimus the way he'd receive a stranger.
Paul covers the money side too. If Onesimus has wronged Philemon or owes him anything, what does Paul say to do?

answers.text: Take it to the church elders

cards.text: With his own hand, Paul writes that he'll repay it, and then, nice and easy: "not to mention that you owe me your very self." He's not mentioning it, friend, he's just putting it in writing IN INK.

cards.question: Remember the hearts Philemon refreshes? Now Paul asks Philemon to refresh Paul's own heart in Christ.
Paul tells Philemon he's worried Philemon might not do what he asks.

cards.text: One more request: "prepare a guest room for me." The man is IN CHAINS and he's already booking the room, because he hopes that "through your prayers I will be restored to you."

cards.question: Paul closes with greetings from the people with him, starting with Epaphras. What does Paul call Epaphras?

answers.text: His fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus
His messenger to all the churches
His host for the whole journey

cards.text: Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke send greetings too, all of them Paul's fellow workers. And Paul signs off: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "our beloved fellow worker.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 17 quotes "prepare a guest room for me.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Onesimus first appears as just "someone named Onesimus." The card never says who he is: Philemon's slave, who was separated from him, as Philemon 1:15-16 makes clear. The baker only learns how Onesimus is tied to Philemon from the question on card 10, so the reason for the letter is unclear for most of the stop.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, "While he was in chains," is a circumstance. Both wrong answers, "While he was in Jerusalem" and "While he was in Antioch," are places. The odd one out stands out, and since Stop 1 already established that Paul is a prisoner, the baker can pick it without reasoning about the passage.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This card covers Philemon 1:21 only as Paul's confidence. It leaves out that Paul knows Philemon will do "even more than I ask," and no other card tells it. That is a key point in Paul's appeal for Onesimus, and the baker leaves without it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
